A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AgentStudio and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–G. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original model and human evaluations on 205 online tasks, alongside GroundUI, IDMBench, and CriticBench experiments and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including online task success rates, grounding accuracy, action-labeling results, and success-detection metrics.

M1.justification: The environment, observation/action spaces, task construction, and annotation procedures remain unchanged. Appendix F.9 explains implementation properties without reporting a revised architecture or procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 205 online tasks and GroundUI, IDMBench, and CriticBench datasets. Appendix F.8 explains existing software choices and potential Photoshop applicability, without reporting additional evaluated software or tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the corresponding experiments. Table 1 retains Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o, both Gemini 1.5 models, and humans; the grounding, action-labeling, and critic comparisons also retain their model sets.

E3.justification: Dataset sampling, metrics, model versions, prompts, greedy decoding, and execution limits match. Appendix F.9 adds deployment discussion without revising the reported experimental settings.

E4.justification: Failure-mode analyses, GUI/API comparisons, the recaptioning ablation in Figure 6, element-size analysis in Figure 7, and Appendix F case studies are retained unchanged. The new subsections add explanations without new analysis evidence.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point-estimate reporting. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, seed variation, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings, and worked examples match. For example, Table 1 retains total success rates of 36.6% for Claude 3.5 Sonnet, 35.6% for GPT-4o, and 72.2% for humans. Appendix results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, observation/action spaces, reward and feedback definitions, and grounding and trajectory task definitions remain identical. No theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a general interactive environment, supporting tools, online tasks, and three capability-specific datasets. Their scientific scope and principal findings are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix F.8 adds software-selection rationale and discusses transferring GIMP tasks to Photoshop. F.9 adds explanations of runtime bottlenecks, resource dependence, scalability, and isolation. The existing result interpretations and Section 7 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix F.9 adds operational details about Docker resources, concurrent instances, frontend/backend separation, and Google-account isolation. The project-page address changes. Docker use and optional human confirmation were already disclosed in v2.

R1.justification: Appendix F.9 adds an explicit Docker-versus-virtual-machine comparison with the already cited OSWorld, refining the existing lightweight-implementation positioning. Section 6 and the bibliography otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Two short subsections, F.8 and F.9, are added. Other edits update affiliations and publication headers, adjust punctuation, and remove duplicated wording from Table 7's caption. The overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is reduced in size, main-text displays reflow, and Table 14 is repositioned below the new appendix discussion. Table 7's caption is corrected. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: The new software-selection rationale and deployment explanations in F.8–F.9 improve transparency and practical understanding, while small editorial corrections improve presentation. These additions remain qualitative and leave the experimental evidence and existing limitations unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
